newsitem.title: USA: ConEd cleared to offer natgas services.
newsitem.headline: ConEd cleared to offer natgas services.

text.p: Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc said Thursday it has been cleared to offer its natural gas customers a range of competitive services, including a choice of suppliers, tailored pricing, appliance repair and financing.
The utility said these services were part of a rate agreement approved Wednesday by the New York Public Service Commission which freezes its base rates through 2000.
As part of the agreement, Con Edison did not implement a $36.1 million per year, 4.1 percent, rate increase that was scheduled to become effective on October 1, 1996.
This would have been the third, and final, installment of the increase approved for the company under its previous rate case, a spokesman said.

The commission said the rate plan was proposed by its staff and the company after discussions with the State Consumer Protection Board, New York City agencies and the New York Oil Heating Association.

The plan includes earnings reductions for Con Edison should the utility fail to meet certain performance criteria, including how successful it is in implementing a program to reduce expenses, the commission said.
It said the plan limits increases in the company's natural gas revenues to covering inflation, if it exceeds four percent during any of the plan's four years.
The plan also establishes a formula under which customers will share in profits from Con Edison's success in the competitive marketplace, the commission said.
The utility said this decision begins implementation of a 1996 order allowing natural gas customers to purchase natural gas from suppliers other than their local utility.
The ConEd spokesman said the utility has been meeting with firms interested in being third party suppliers and has requested tariff changes from the commission suggested by the potential suppliers.

The commission said it has required Con Edison to file within 30 days a plan allowing for further unbundling of its rates. "Unbundling" refers to the process of taking a rate for a combined service and pricing them separately.

The spokesman said tailored pricing will allow the company to negotiate individual pricing arrangements with customers, noting these negotiations would be conducted only with ConEd's largest customers. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
